title: Ukraine unleashes more than 400 drones near Moscow in one of war's biggest attacks
summary: More than 400 drones targeted Moscow in one of Ukraine's largest attacks, striking an oil depot and logistics facilities more than 250 miles from the border.
story: Russian officials say two people were wounded and buildings caught fire after one of the largest drone attacks on the Moscow region. (Reuters.)

Ukraine launched one of its largest drone attacks of the war against Moscow and the surrounding region overnight, striking an oil depot and logistics facilities more than 250 miles from the Ukrainian border, according to Ukrainian and Russian officials.

Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 400 Ukrainian drones were launched toward the Moscow region between Sunday evening and early Monday, including 85 that were destroyed while approaching the Russian capital. Russia’s Defense Ministry separately claimed that its forces intercepted 381 drones across Russian regions, the Black Sea and the Sea of Azov.
The Russian claims could not be independently verified by Fox News Digital.

At least 10 people were wounded in the Moscow region, including three Chinese nationals, according to regional authorities cited by Reuters. Seven of the injuries were reported in Domodedovo, Russia, where officials said a residential building was struck and a fire broke out at an industrial park near one of Moscow’s main airports.
The scale and reach of the operation suggest Ukraine is moving beyond occasional symbolic attacks on Moscow and building a sustained campaign against the infrastructure that supports Russia’s war.
UKRAINE LAUNCHES WHAT APPEARS TO BE ONE OF ITS LARGEST DRONE ATTACKS AGAINST RUSSIA: REPORT

By simultaneously targeting oil facilities, transportation networks and logistics hubs hundreds of miles from the front, Kyiv is seeking to disrupt the flow of fuel and supplies to Russian forces, reduce revenue available to the Kremlin and force Moscow to divert air-defense systems away from the battlefield.
Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries had doubled since the beginning of 2026, Reuters reported, contributing to refinery shutdowns and reduced production of gasoline, diesel and jet fuel.
Smoke and flames rise from an industrial facility in Podolsk, Russia, in the Moscow region, after a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack overnight July 20, 2026. (East2west news)
President Volodymyr Zelenskyy confirmed that Ukrainian forces targeted logistics facilities and an oil depot in the Moscow region.

"Our long-range sanctions have produced results against logistics facilities and an oil depot," Zelenskyy wrote on X, adding that the targets were more than 400 kilometers (roughly 250 miles) from Ukraine’s border. "We are responding, justly, to every Russian strike against our cities and communities."

Wildberries, a company known as "Russia’s Amazon," said its logistics center in the Podolsk district of Russia was temporarily evacuated as a precaution before resuming normal operations, East2West News reported. Ukraine has accused the company of selling supplies used by the Russian military.
RUSSIA UNLEASHES NEARLY 600 MISSILES AND DRONES ON KYIV IN DEADLIEST STRIKE SINCE MAY

Smoke rises from the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Golden Leo after it was struck near Odesa on July 20, 2026. Ukrainian officials said 10 people were killed in the Russian missile attack. (East2west news)

Ksenia Svetlova, associate fellow at Chatham House policy institute based in London, argued that the disruption caused by strikes on fuel infrastructure and companies such as Wildberries is unlikely, by itself, to change President Vladimir Putin’s approach to the war.

"The hardship of the Russian citizen who suffers because of fuel shortages, the strike on a Wildberries warehouse, or forced recruitment does not interest him," Svetlova said. "The war machine is operating at full force, and he has neither the desire nor the ability to stop it."

Svetlova said Putin remains reluctant to announce another mass mobilization after large numbers of young Russians fled the country during the Kremlin’s previous call-up. At the same time, she said, Russia’s military still needs additional troops after recruiting heavily from its prison population and is increasingly pressuring ordinary civilians accused of relatively minor offenses to sign military contracts.

The sweeping Ukrainian operation followed one of Russia’s largest ballistic missile attacks of the war against Kyiv. Ukraine’s air force said Russia launched 41 missiles of various types in the overnight barrage, which killed at least one person and wounded 16, Reuters reported Sunday.
The Russian attack also spread into the Black Sea, where a Russian missile attack on the Guinea-Bissau-flagged cargo ship Golden Leo killed 10 people near Odesa, Reuters reported Monday.
'A NEW KIND OF WAR': INSIDE UKRAINE'S HIDDEN FACTORIES MASS-PRODUCING COMBAT DRONES
An explosion strikes a building in Domodedovo, in the Moscow region, during a large-scale Ukrainian drone attack overnight on July 20, 2026. (East2West news)

Ukrainian officials said the vessel, which was carrying corn, was struck by three cruise missiles and caught fire. Nine crew members and a Ukrainian maritime pilot were killed, while eight other crew members were rescued. The ship’s crew included Indian and Syrian nationals, according to Reuters.

The escalation comes as Zelenskyy faces growing domestic pressure over his removal of Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, a 35-year-old reformer credited with expanding Ukraine’s drone capabilities and seeking to modernize military procurement and management. Fedorov’s supporters viewed him as a rare official willing to challenge entrenched practices, improve oversight of defense spending and push a technology-centered approach to the war.

Thousands of demonstrators gathered following Fedorov’s dismissal, demanding his reinstatement and the removal of commander-in-chief Gen. Oleksandr Syrskyi. Protesters have accused Syrskyi of resisting modernization and retaining a rigid command structure that they say contributes to high troop losses. Syrskyi has defended his wartime record and called for unity.

Fedorov publicly accused Syrskyi of blocking his initiatives and sabotaging his work. Zelenskyy said their relationship had deteriorated so badly that the two could no longer work together, but provided little additional explanation for removing Fedorov.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
People protest against Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy's decision to replace Mykhailo Fedorov as defense minister in Kyiv, Ukraine, July 18, 2026. (Thomas Peter/Reuters)

Zelenskyy indicated Monday that consultations over Ukraine’s military leadership were continuing, saying he had spoken with Maj. Gen. Mykhailo Drapatyi about ensuring that the experience of every branch of Ukraine’s defense forces was applied in a coordinated manner. He did not announce any decision on Syrskyi’s future.
Reuters contributed to this report.

title: Andy Burnham takes over as UK prime minister, calls for 'new political model'
summary: Andy Burnham enters Downing Street vowing to shift power away from London, but his past criticism of Trump could create early friction with Washington.
story: New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledges major socialist changes, including nationalizing utilities, expanding government housing and re-industrializing Britain.

New British Prime Minister Andy Burnham assumed power Monday morning, vowing to move authority away from London as his new government confronts economic strain, political instability and potential friction with Washington.

"We will change politics, to make it more collaborative, more about problem-solving than point scoring," Burnham said outside 10 Downing Street. "And we will take power out of here and carry it into every postcode in the land, so that they can do more.

"And, in doing more, build a new economy where we put life's essentials back under stronger public control to make them affordable to you again – reindustrializing Britain, using public procurement to back British industry."

Burnham, 56, was greeted by King Charles III at Buckingham Palace, London, on Monday before his swearing-in and first remarks. King Charles formally requested that Burnham form a new administration, and Burnham accepted.
WHO IS ANDY BURNHAM? THE TRUMP CRITIC SET TO BECOME THE UK'S NEXT PRIME MINISTER

Andy Burnham delivers his inaugural speech as the U.K.'s new prime minister on July 20, 2026, in London. He becomes the U.K.'s 59th prime minister, succeeding Sir Keir Starmer. (Dan Kitwood/Getty Images)

"I have just come from Buckingham Palace, where I have accepted His Majesty the King's invitation to form a government," Burnham's brief introduction began. "And in doing so, I am acutely conscious that I am the sixth person in the last 10 years to walk up this street – the seventh prime minister since 2016, making this a moment for reflection and new resolution.

"It requires my generation of politicians to raise our game and rise to the new challenge. Britain needs to show the world that we can regain our stability once again, and that is our challenge to make politics work, to make it work better," he said.
"I know people at home are fed up with politics. I hear you and I want to be honest with you: We have not been good enough, and we need to be better. We will be."
Burnham called for sweeping political and economic changes.
UK PM ANDY BURNHAM REJECTS THATCHER-ERA POLICIES, SIGNALS LEFTWARD SHIFT

New Prime Minister Andy Burnham is welcomed by King Charles III during an audience at Buckingham Palace in London on Monday, July 20, 2026. Burnham was invited to become prime minister and form a new government. (PA Wire/PA Images)
"We will make this moment a circuit breaker for Britain, bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years," he said. "A new political model and a new economic model.
"In the 1980s, Britain took some wrong turns. Political power was centralized, economic power privatized, large parts of the country deindustrialized, and they still haven't recovered.
"Many feel as though they're still in decline, and they don't have the ability to turn things around."
Burnham vowed to "bring forward a new plan for Britain."

"A 10-year plan, laying out a path from where we are now to where I believe we all want Britain to be – wherever we're coming from, whatever party we support," he said. "But I can do something to give people some breathing space now, some help with the cost of living. And I will set out some of those measures starting tomorrow, including how we pay for them.

"We will help more young people into work by changing the education system and giving them more support, more mental health support, and we will build more council homes. That is the fair and sustainable way to bring the welfare bill down to meet our fiscal rules and to honor our commitments on defense to our international partners."
ANDY BURNHAM ELECTED LABOUR LEADER, SET TO BECOME UK PRIME MINISTER
Prime Minister Andy Burnham assumes the leadership role without being elected, a fact not lost on critics of his democratic-socialist agenda. (Christopher Furlong/Getty Images)
His first order of business in office will be "to end rough sleeping in our country."
"It's about putting the right values and the right standards at the heart of government," he concluded. "I will put the care of people at the heart of everything I do.

"I will give this my all and I ask you all to pull with me. Let's build a new national sense of unity, of common purpose and positivity. Let us make this the moment when Britain starts to believe again, the moment we bring back hope. Thank you very much, everybody."
Outgoing Keir Starmer officially submitted his resignation and passed "the baton" in remarks outside 10 Downing Street.
BRITISH PRIME MINISTER KEIR STARMER FACES POTENTIAL LEADERSHIP CHALLENGE FROM NEWLY-ELECTED ANDY BURNHAM

Outgoing Labor Prime Minister Keir Starmer bid farewell to office Monday morning outside 10 Downing Street: "As I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham, I wish him every success: He has my full support." (Carl Court/Getty Images)
"As I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham, I wish him every success," Starmer said. "He has my full support.

"For all the focus on individuals, politics will always be a team sport and the changes we have delivered for our country and our party belong to everyone who has fought for them. I thank them again today, and I thank the British people for the opportunity to serve.
"I go with good grace, I go with a smile, and I go proud of everything that we have achieved."
STARMER IN 'SEISMIC' CRISIS, UK DEFENSE CHIEF QUITS BEFORE HIGH-STAKES TRUMP NATO SUMMIT

Burnham's relationship with Washington could provide an early foreign-policy test. He has repeatedly criticized Trump, comparing the instability surrounding the president’s return to office with the turmoil under former British Prime Minister Liz Truss and warning against importing what he called America’s polarized political culture.
He has maintained that the U.S.-U.K. relationship remains important, though, pledging continuity on NATO, Britain’s nuclear deterrent and support for Ukraine.

Trump previously dismissed Burnham as the former "mayor of a town" and said he had heard the incoming British leader was "extremely liberal." Reform UK has also challenged Burnham’s mandate, arguing that he should call a general election after reaching Downing Street without facing either a competitive Labor leadership contest or a nationwide vote.
KEIR STARMER REPORTEDLY CONSIDERING STEPPING DOWN AS PM AND COULD ANNOUNCE TIMETABLE FOR DEPARTURE

Burnham succeeds Starmer after becoming Labor leader unopposed Friday. He enters office without a new national vote under Britain’s parliamentary system, which allows the governing party to change leaders midterm. The next general election is not required until 2029, though Burnham could call one earlier.

At the center of his agenda is what he calls "Manchesterism" — an effort to give cities and regions greater authority over transportation, housing, infrastructure and economic development. He has paired that approach with what he describes as "business-friendly socialism," combining greater public control of essential services with cooperation between government and private industry.

Burnham's arrival at Downing Street caps a decade-long political comeback. After losing his second Labor leadership contest in 2015, Burnham left national politics and built a new power base in Greater Manchester, where nine years as mayor earned him the nickname "King of the North" and a reputation as an effective communicator willing to challenge the government in London.
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
"I will work to build a new politics; the country is crying out for it," he said Friday. "People are looking for us to deliver, and we will."
Reuters and Fox News' Efrat Lachter contributed to this report.

Eric Mack is a breaking news reporter and writer Sunday through Thursday, 6 a.m. ET to 2 p.m. ET, with a particular interest in stories that lead the news cycle on politics, elections, foreign affairs and government.

title: Steve Forbes urges Trump to keep the Strait of Hormuz open at all costs
summary: Publisher Steve Forbes calls for maximum pressure on Tehran regime, urges Trump administration to keep the Strait of Hormuz open as a non-negotiable imperative.
story: Publisher Steve Forbes argues the Strait of Hormuz is a strategic asset that must remain open at all costs, advises Trump to keep all options on the table in dealing with Iran
Steve Forbes says the United States must double down on efforts to topple the Tehran regime, arguing that free passage through the Strait of Hormuz should remain a non-negotiable American imperative.

As the U.S. struck targets in Iran for a ninth consecutive day on Sunday, pressure on the Tehran regime continued to build. Speaking at Freedom Fest in Las Vegas, the chairman and editor-in-chief of Forbes and former presidential candidate sat down with Fox News Digital to discuss Iran and the Trump administration's foreign policy.
STEVE FORBES BACKS TRUMP'S MT. RUSHMORE WARNING ON COMMUNISM: 'HE'S RIGHT'
"Get Iran done with. No more fake ceasefires. Get rid of that evil regime," Steve Forbes said. (Fox News)

"Going back to Thomas Jefferson, a core foreign policy plank of the United States is freedom of the seas. Freedom of navigation got us into another war with Great Britain, the War of 1812," Forbes said.
"So we've been doing it for over two centuries. The Strait of Hormuz is an international waterway, just as the South China Sea is an international waterway. And so we must keep that open.

August 1804: Tracers arc in the sky as ships of the U.S. navy bombard Tripoli in an action against a ruler who supported the Tripolitan (Barbary) pirates. The pirates demanded protection money from all ships and the USA decided to go to war to release their hold on the area.  (MPI/Getty Images)
"No tolls, no restrictions, all ships of commerce should have free passage through it unmolested."

Forbes said that with proper application of air power, boots on the ground wouldn't be needed, but he would not discard that as an option, bringing the example of the engagement with the Barbary pirates, which brought freedom of navigation to the Mediterranean following the completion of the First Barbary War of 1805.
TWO US SERVICE MEMBERS KILLED IN IRANIAN STRIKES ON JORDAN, CENTCOM SAYS
The U.S. military has been enforcing a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz, even during the ceasefire. (U.S. Central Command)

"If we do things right in the air, that won't be necessary. But as we demonstrated with the Barbary pirates, sometimes you do need hand-to-hand combat. But again, with our great military and the great Israeli military, we should be able to bring this evil regime down and enable the elements in the Iranian army that want change to feel we're not going to pull the rug out from under them with another fake ceasefire. That we keep hammering away at this evil regime."
A container ship, right, and a cargo vessel are seen in the Strait of Hormuz off Bandar Abbas, Iran, June 17, 2026. (Amirhosein Khorgooi/ISNA via AP)
Ultimately, Forbes said freedom of navigation should be an international red line:

"So the key thing is, if you don't enforce these key principles of freedom of navigation, liberty, you're going to lose them. Ronald Reagan was right. Others have made the same observation. You have to preserve liberty each and every generation."
President Ronald Reagan gives a speech from the Oval Office of the White House. (Diana Walker/Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP
Forbes said the time for diplomacy with Tehran has passed, and encouraged the Trump administration to ratchet up the pressure, while also praising a recent decision on Ukraine policy.

"Get Iran done with. No more fake ceasefires. Get rid of that evil regime. By the way, I'm delighted that he's saying he's going to give licensing for Patriot missiles to Ukraine. That'll bring a good result there."
David Unsworth reports on Latin America. You can follow David Unsworth on Twitter @LatinAmerUpdate

title: Ex-counterterrorism official Joe Kent continues calling for US military withdrawal from Middle East
summary: Former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent is continuing to advocate for the withdrawal of U.S. forces from the Middle East.
story: 'The Big Weekend Show' co-hosts discuss CENTCOM's announcement of a ninth straight night of strikes against Iran.
Former National Counterterrorism Center Director Joe Kent is reiterating his call for the withdrawal of US forces from the Middle East amid the ongoing war with Iran.

"Get our troops out now before we suffer a mass casualty attack. Break the escalation trap. Trump still has the political strength at home to declare victory & have it resonate, that ability will be lost if we suffer more casualties. Now is the time to leave, immediately," he wrote Sunday on X.
Kent made the comments while sharing a post from U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM).

"Yesterday, U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) announced the passing of two U.S. service members and the missing status of one in Jordan following an Iranian attack on July 17. After a thorough search, U.S. military personnel found unidentified remains at the location earlier today. An examination process to verify the remains is ongoing," CENTCOM noted in part of a statement on Sunday.

"Separately, a U.S. service member in northern Iraq was killed in action July 18 during a controlled detonation of unexploded ordnance from a downed Iranian one-way attack drone. A second service member was wounded and continues to receive medical treatment for a minor injury," the statement noted.
US SERVICE MEMBER KILLED IN IRAQ AS TROOPS RECOVER UNIDENTIFIED REMAINS IN JORDAN: CENTCOM
President Donald Trump steps off Air Force One upon arrival at John F. Kennedy International Airport in New York, N.Y. on July 17, 2026. (Mandel NGAN / AFP via Getty Images)
A White House spokesperson on Monday pointed Fox News Digital to comments President Donald Trump had made on Sunday.
"Well, we feel very badly. But you know those great people, those great patriots were out there fighting that Iran cannot have a nuclear weapon," he said.

"Iran has been very, very badly damaged," he said, asserting that the foreign nation has "lost everything, almost, militarily. They've got very little left. They've got some missiles.  They've got some drones.  They've got some manufacturing ability — not much," he said. "We control the Strait.  They don't control anything.  So we'll see what happens. But we hit 'em very hard again tonight," he said, adding that "we did that in honor of the probably three — it’s probably three, as opposed to two — great patriots."
EX-COUNTERTERRORISM OFFICIAL JOE KENT ENDORSES GOP SENATE PRIMARY CHALLENGER AS TRUMP BACKS LINDSEY GRAHAM
Kent quit the counterterrorism government post earlier this year, citing his opposition to the Iran war.
In part of his resignation letter he asserted, "Iran posed no imminent threat to our nation, and it is clear that we started this war due to pressure from Israel and its powerful American lobby."
EX-COUNTERTERRORISM CHIEF WARNS OF 'MAJOR PROBLEM' THAT COULD FORCE US 'BACK INTO THE WAR ON IRAN'S TERMS'

Joseph Kent, director of the National Counterterrorism Center, during a House Homeland Security Committee hearing in Washington, D.C., on Thursday, Dec. 11, 2025. (Daniel Heuer/Bloomberg via Getty Images)
CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

In a portion of a Saturday post on X he wrote, "We restore order by ending the conflict on our terms: deprive Iran of military targets to strike by removing our troops, bases, & naval forces from the area. Our bases in the region are liabilities & relics of the past—abandoning them is not retreat, it’s strategic adaptation to modern warfare. This move removes Iran’s primary justification for disrupting shipping in the SOH and for attacking its neighbors. We can then offer the carrot: sanctions relief in exchange for freedom of navigation in the SOH."
Alex Nitzberg is a writer for Fox News Digital.

title: Influencer killed by husband after she accused him of pedophilia on TikTok
summary: Social media influencer Sara Gilson was killed by her estranged husband less than two weeks after she posted on TikTok accusing him of pedophilia, according to police and court records.
story: A social media influencer was killed by her estranged husband less than two weeks after she posted on TikTok accusing him of pedophilia, according to police and court records.

Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Sara Gilson was fatally shot Thursday in Owasso, Oklahoma, by husband Jeremiah Duffey, who went by Shawn Duffey on social media, according to the Owasso Police Department. She was 43.
A little over a month earlier, on June 10, she filed and was granted an emergency protective order against Duffey after police informed her he’d been accused the day prior of molesting a minor.
On July 11, Gilson posted a video on TikTok, where she had more than 30,000 followers, accusing Duffey of pedophilia.
“Preparing for when Netflix drops a documentary about my soon to be ex husband who I just found out is a pedophile,” Gilson wrote.

The video referenced a popular social media trend that mimics Netflix documentaries, with users pretending to sit for a tell-all interview. Her caption read: “I wish I was joking. #plottwist #netflix #documentary.”
Less than two weeks later, Gilson was killed.

On June 9, about a month before Gilson posted the video, a girl and a parent told police that Duffey, who coached the girl’s traveling basketball team, inappropriately touched her during an event at an elementary school earlier that evening, police said. Another team coach saw what happened and immediately intervened and reported it to the girl’s parent, police said.

“Similar conduct by this coach towards this particular juvenile player was reported to have occurred over an extended period of time, in multiple law enforcement jurisdictions, across multiple states prior to this incident,” police said Saturday.
Duffey fled and had not been seen by police since.

Because Duffey was a member of the Osage tribe and the incident at the school happened on tribal land, police said, they submitted the case for a charge of lewd molestation of a minor to the U.S. Attorney’s Office for review, “ending the jurisdiction of the Owasso Police Department over this reported incident.”
Following the report, police contacted Gilson and gave her information on how to seek an emergency protective order.

She did just that and the order was granted June 10, Tulsa County court records show. Duffey was ordered to stay 100 yards away from Gilson and her home at all times. The attorney who represented Duffey did not immediately respond to a request for comment Saturday.

On Thursday, officers responded to a domestic violence incident at a residence in the city of Collinsville at 11:16 p.m. after a 911 call in which dispatchers heard a woman screaming followed by “what sounded to be a gunshot,” police said. Dispatchers attempted to call back but got no answer.

Moments later, a boy called 911 from a neighbor’s home and said his stepfather had shot his mother, police said. When officers arrived at the home, they found Gilson and Duffey dead from apparent gunshot wounds to the head, police said.
Police are still investigating, but they said the deaths appear to be a murder-suicide.
Gilson’s son was taken into protective custody and later released to a parent who wasn’t involved in the incident, authorities said. Gilson leaves behind the son and a daughter.

“Sara was an incredible mom. Her children were the center of her world, and everything she did was for them,” an online fundraiser set up for the kids said. “She loved them fiercely, worked hard to provide for them, and dreamed of giving them the best life possible.”
If you or someone you know is in crisis, call or text 988 or go to 988lifeline.org to reach the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline, or visit SpeakingOfSuicide.com/resources.

title: Rick Moranis ends retirement with surprise Comic-Con appearance for ‘Spaceballs 2’
summary: Lord Dark Helmet is so back!
story: Lord Dark Helmet is so back!
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

During a panel for the upcoming sequel to the 1987 “Star Wars” parody film “Spaceballs” at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, Rick Moranis, who played the hilarious spoof on Darth Vader, made a special appearance.
The 73-year-old, who is reprising his role for the sequel, donned his iconic enormous helmet from the original film and walked through the packed house at Hall H of the San Diego Convention Center.
The crowd couldn’t help but give Moranis, who stepped back from appearing in films almost three decades ago, a standing ovation.

The sequel, entitled “Spaceballs: The New One,” is slated to hit theaters on April 23, 2027. The project was championed by several comedians and actors including Josh Gad. It will feature some familiar faces, like the original film’s director Mel Brooks, who is not only a producer on the sequel but also reprising his role as the beloved Yoda parody character Yogurt.

Moranis’ entrance was certainly a theatrical one. The actor did not begin the event with the rest of the panel. Rather, he surprised the crowd by popping up in the audience after being hidden under the helmet. The crowd, understandably, went wild.
Moranis, who then joined the panel, told fans about his decision to reenter the industry with the upcoming film.
“It just felt like this is it. It’s time,” he told the crowd. “I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made.”
The actor, whose reprisal of the beloved villain role was announced last year, also joked that he had never really left. He said that he had discussed the idea of a sequel way back in 1989.
“I wasn’t really retired,” he joked. “I was just negotiating.”
The panel was filled with several other noteworthy moments, including a parody of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the universe of Marvel superhero films that are typically released in “phases.”
For this event, the panel unveiled the “Spaceballs Cinematic Universe.” The MCU spoof included upwards of 11 phases including “The Almighty Schwartz Saga.” (IYKYK!)
Though Mel Brooks, who recently turned 100, did not attend the event, he sent along a hilarious video message.

“Sorry I can’t be with you. I’m on the convention floor trying to buy a rare Charizard card. When I was your age, on a Friday, I would go to something called ‘work,’” he said in the video, according to Deadline. “From the bottom of my heart I want to say, thank you, nerds.”

title: ‘Cockroaches won’: India’s youth protest leaders declare victory as minister resigns
summary: India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protests on Saturday after the country’s education minister resigned and the government agreed to a number of the activist movement’s demands.
story: India’s viral Cockroach Janta Party called off its nationwide protests on Saturday after the country’s education minister resigned and the government agreed to a number of the activist movement’s demands.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Dharmendra Pradhan announced his resignation on X after talks with the CJP, which has demanded major reforms after the handling of an alleged exam paper leak triggered one of India’s biggest displays of public dissent in recent years, including one activist’s 26-day hunger strike.

“I hold deep respect for the aspirations, sentiments, and rightful expectations of the youth of this country,” Pradhan wrote on X. “Realising the dreams of India’s young generation has been the moral resolve of our political and social life.”

Ministers JP Nadda and Jitendra Singh later told a press conference all police cases against protesters would be dropped and the government will pay compensation to the families of students who died by suicide after the alleged paper leaks, according to Reuters news agency. The government will also consider the CJP’s proposals for reforms to exams, the group said.

The CJP, a viral movement that began as an online parody of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP), confirmed it had called off its protests because all of its major demands “have been accepted by the government.”
“Cockroaches won. Democracy won!” it said on X.
In New Delhi, crowds of students and activists were celebrating in the streets following the announcement, many of them waving Indian flags.
The scandal has been growing since May, when online leaks disrupted the NEET undergraduate exam, the fiercely competitive gateway to India’s medical schools.

Anger among India’s young people has exploded onto the streets in recent weeks, with protests spreading from New Delhi to other cities around the country, including Mumbai, Hyderabad, Bengaluru and Ahmedabad. Authorities have struggled to contain the growing protests, with police deploying tear gas and batons against the vast crowds close to the country’s Parliament building in New Delhi earlier this week.

The CJP, named after a remark from India’s Chief Justice Surya Kant comparing unemployed young people to “cockroaches,” became the center of what has been one of the biggest challenges to Modi in his 12 years in power.

As well as the minister’s resignation, protesters’ demands included compensation for the families of students who died by suicide after the exam paper leaks, and accountability over police suppression of their protests.
“Remember, do not mess with cockroaches,” it posted Saturday.
What's behind India’s Gen Z ‘cockroach’ movement

On Thursday night, Modi offered his first public comments in a video posted to Instagram. “I know the paper leak is not a trivial matter,” he said, announcing fast-track courts to prosecute cases involving examination paper leaks, while defending his government’s handling of the scandal.

But protesters said his response fell short of their demands for accountability and hundreds of people returned to the streets of New Delhi on Friday even as authorities shut 18 stations across the city’s metro network, disrupting a vital mode of transportation for its 23 million residents.

A 26-day hunger strike by activist Sonam Wangchuk had further galvanized the protests this week, after police forcefully admitted him to a hospital last weekend. He said in a post on X Friday that he ended his fast after appeals from dozens of members of Parliament and following “a long negotiation on various conditions and in view of possible violence in the country.”
Wangchuk on Saturday called Pradhan’s resignation “a victory of peace, patience & perseverance.”
“Congratulations CJP, Gen Z of the nation and thank you all citizens for shedding fear and the fear of fear and rising up from every corner of the nation,” he posted on X.

title: Bags in vehicle of man fatally shot by ICE did not contain drugs, Texas DA says
summary: HOUSTON — A substance investigators found in a van driven by a man fatally shot by ICE earlier this month was not an illegal narcotic, the Harris County District Attorney’s Office said Friday.
story: HOUSTON — A substance investigators found in a van driven by a man fatally shot by ICE earlier this month was not an illegal narcotic, the Harris County District Attorney’s Office said Friday.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.

Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, a 51-year-old father of three, was fatally shot by an ICE law enforcement officer during a July 7 traffic stop the agency said turned life-threatening. The government has alleged he weaponized the vehicle, but that argument has been disputed by others in the van.

After the fatal shooting, an FBI agent said small bags consistent with drug packaging that contained a substance resembling methamphetamine could be seen in plain view inside the vehicle. The bureau obtained a search warrant, allowing agents to search the van.

The Harris County District Attorney’s Office said Friday on X that the seized substance “tested negative for narcotics/ illicit drugs.” It said it would not comment further on the results, citing the pending investigation.
“We have notified Salgado Araujo’s family because we felt they had the right to know,” the DA’s office said.
Add NBC News to Google
Add NBC News to Google
David Donatti, senior staff attorney at the ACLU of Texas, said in a statement Friday that Salgado Araujo was a “hardworking man” who built houses for Texas families.

“The government has demonstrated that it is more interested in creating a false narrative than in seeking the truth,” he said of the search warrant. “The Salgados deserve real answers about what happened.”

Ruby L. Powers, a lawyer who represents Victor Salgado Araujo, Salgado Araujo’s brother who was taken into custody following the shooting, said previously that the substance was believed to be “granulated salt, which is paired with lemon and water as a homemade electrolyte mix used by outdoor workers in extreme Texas heat.”
Powers said Friday that full lab results expected next week will confirm what the substance was.

“An unproven claim was allowed to circulate before it was tested, and the way it was made public did real damage, diverting attention from what actually matters in this case,” she said. “Lorenzo was shot, and no lab report answers for that.”
ICE referred a request for comment on the district attorney’s finding to the Department of Homeland Security, which did not immediately respond. The FBI said it has no comment.
Caucus hearing on shooting

The finding was announced a few hours after the Congressional Hispanic Caucus held a hearing on the shooting Friday in Houston and addressed the search warrant application for the van that Salgado Araujo was driving.
Along with members of the caucus, Rep. Bennie Thompson, the ranking member on the House Homeland Security Comittee, also attended.

Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare said during the hearing that drug involvement would have been out of character for any of the people in the van that morning. The unsealing of the FBI’s search warrant request before a grand jury could see the investigation’s evidence was unprecedented in his career.
“To unseal it the day it’s signed, never seen it in my 20 years,” he said during the hearing.
Lawyer Hugo Balderas-Ibarra, who represents two others who were in the van, said in a statement Friday that the possibility Salgado Araujo was involved in any way with drugs is “absurd.”
Lorenzo Salgado Jr., one of Salgado Araujo’s sons, testified at the hearing, criticizing ICE and its parent agency, the Department of Homeland Security.

“Over the past two weeks we’ve had to grieve our father too soon,” he said. “DHS first said ICE targeted our father, then admitted he was never their intended target at all. DHS also said he weaponized his vehicle, a claim the three men who were in the van with him have directly disputed and one that surveillance footage, so far, does not appear to show.”
ICE personnel at the scene did not have body cameras, DHS said, and any possible security or cellphone video of the confrontation, if it exists, has not been released.

title: Tony Romo arrested and booked on suspicion of impaired driving in Milwaukee
summary: CBS football analyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo was arrested Thursday night in Milwaukee on suspicion of intoxicated driving, officials said.
story: CBS football analyst and former Dallas Cowboys quarterback Tony Romo was arrested Thursday night in Milwaukee on suspicion of intoxicated driving, officials said.
Subscribe to read this story ad-free
Get unlimited access to ad-free articles and exclusive content.
Romo, 46, was pulled over on southbound Interstate 43 at about 6:18 p.m. CT after he “performed poorly” on standardized field sobriety tests,  according to Milwaukee County Sheriff’s records.
Romo was booked on one count of allegedly operating while intoxicated and released.

He was ordered to appear in court on Sept. 21, which would be the Monday night of the NFL’s Week 2. The top CBS matchup of that weekend figures to be the Pittsburgh Steelers visiting the AFC -champion New England Patriots.
The stop came just hours after Romo wrapped up a golf course  interview with NBC affiliate WTMJ, the Milwaukee TV station reported.

Romo was back in town to play in the Wisconsin Amateur Championship at the West Bend Country Club. He shot a four-round total of 319, good for a 73rd place tie, 32 strokes back of tournament champ Spencer Turtz.
A cheerful Romo said he takes golf seriously, but appreciates that spinning a football was and probably still is his better skill.
“I’m competitive in both,” Romo told the station. “I am just better at football. But I think we’re gaining strides.”
Romo played in parts of 13 seasons in the NFL, all for the Dallas Cowboys, before seamlessly transitioning to the booth with CBS.
He’s one-third of the network’s top NFL broadcast team, alongside play-by-play announcer Jim Nantz and sideline reporter Tracy Wolfson. Romo called his third Super Bowl in 2024.
Romo said he respects the passion of NFL fans and hopes to add to their enjoyment every Sunday.

“For me, it is always making the viewer learn something or enjoy the telecast,” Romo told TMJ4 sports director Karley Marotta. “It’s their team. This is a huge deal. I always want them to understand, I get that.”
It wasn’t immediately clear Friday whether Romo had hired a defense attorney to speak on his behalf.
A representative for CBS Sports declined comment Friday.

title: Watch Emeril Lagasse Find Out That He’s Become The Internet’s Latest Obsession
summary: Almost 20 years after his hit Food Network shows “Emeril Live” and “Essence of Emeril” went off the air, internet users are becoming obsessed with Emeril Lagasse.
story: Almost 20 years after his hit Food Network shows “Emeril Live” and “Essence of Emeril” went off the air, internet users are becoming obsessed with Emeril Lagasse. And he’s just gotten the heads up.

Lagasse, 66, shared a video on July 24 in which he finds out that old clips of his shows have been trending across social media. For weeks, the chef has been a hot topic of discussion as millennials and more relive their favorite, often-outrageous moments.
The chef, known for yelling, “BAM!” after hitting his dishes with flavor, is clearly reveling in the nostalgia.
“That’s some good s---,” Lagasse says in the video.

In the clip, Lagasse watches several of his iconic television moments from the height of his fame in the late 1990s and 2000s. There’s of course a snippet from an iconic Halloween episode where he cooks in full-costume, incredible crowd reactions, and a series of iconic “BAM”-filled moments.
Lagasse was one of the mainstays of the Food Network for about a decade. A master of Creole and Cajun cuisine, Lagasse racked up a following for his big personality and hilarious kitchen antics.

Though his most popular show “Emeril Live” came to an end on the Food Network by 2007, Lagasse never really left our television screens. He went on to host several other series including “Emeril’s Florida,” “Emeril Cooks” and more. He also makes frequent appearances on competition cooking show “Top Chef.”

In recent weeks, people have been resurfacing their favorite Lagasse clips. They’ve included one in which he gives into his well-known obsession with garlic, another in which he has the studio audience in absolute awe after he adds two beers to a dish and yet another hilarious one in which he reveals his hack for fixing an overly-thickened sauce.
Social media users haven’t been shy about the impact that the chef has had on their lives.
“I attribute my love of cooking to watching Emeril as a kid in the 90’s,” one person wrote.
Another individual shared that Lagasse “inspired me to become a chef.”
Truthfully, it’s no surprise that he’s been embraced by the internet. Sometimes, you really just have to kick it up a notch.

title: Beatriz Hatz Of ‘Love Island USA’ Wins A National Long Jump Title Weeks After Season 8 Finale
summary: Beatriz Hatz, who was a contestant on “Love Island USA” Season 8, won gold at the USA track and field outdoor national championships for the T64 women’s long jump competition.
story: Beatriz Hatz, who was a contestant on the most recent season of “Love Island USA,” may not have won the reality competition show, but she did just bring home a giant W.

The two-time paralympian, 25, won gold at the USA track and field outdoor national championships in New York City on July 23 for the T64 women’s long jump competition. The title comes just weeks after the show wrapped, with its finale on July 12.

The T64 long jump event is for athletes with movement that’s been “moderately affected” in either one lower leg or the absence of one or both legs below the knee, according to Lexi Global, a platform which explains the rules of para-sports.

While Beatriz started out in second place behind long jumper Taleah Williams, she hit her stride by the fifth round, posting a mark of 5.24 meters, according to ESPN. She secured the top spot after the sixth round with a mark of 5.11 meters.
What’s more, Hatz had some extra special fans in attendance. Season 8 cast mates Sean Reifel and Amora Robinson were there to cheer on their fellow islander.
“Shout out Bea,” Sean said in a video interview, following the event. “She’s a monster.”
Amora is also seen in the video, telling Beatriz after the competition, “We’re so proud of you!”

The results are particularly impressive given Beatriz’s inability to fully train while in the villa. Beatriz was among the original Season 8 cast members. She quickly made a name for herself for her blunt honesty with the other islanders and her jokes about her limb difference. Her time, however, was cut short. And by Episode 9, she left the villa after America voted to pair her then-partner Gabriel with new bombshell Jen Terry.
Beatriz told TODAY.com in a July 22 interview that it was impossible to keep up her usual regimen while on the island.

“My training will take three to four hours, maybe, on the track, depending on what we’re doing and how fast or slow we’re going about things,” she said. “But in the villa, it’s like, you’ve got time to do this, and then you got to go back to doing your other things, like having chats. So I had to be very efficient with the work I was doing.”
However, Beatriz said that she did what she could.
“I took my blade with me. I actually did some training with my blade on. I know they didn’t show it, but I was training,” she said.
Beatriz added that she “did a bunch of long jump drills, like repetitive takeoffs, a lot of technical work in the blade, and I did like a tendon ligament circuit, just as much stuff as I could do.”

title: Rick Moranis Gets Comic-Con Standing Ovation As He Comes Out Of Retirement For ‘Spaceballs 2’
summary: During a panel for the upcoming sequel to the 1987 “Star Wars” parody film “Spaceballs” at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, Rick Moranis made a special appearance as Lord Dark Helmet.
story: Lord Dark Helmet is so back!

During a panel for the upcoming sequel to the 1987 “Star Wars” parody film “Spaceballs” at San Diego Comic-Con on Friday, Rick Moranis, who played the hilarious spoof on Darth Vader, made a special appearance.
The 73-year-old, who is reprising his role for the sequel, donned his iconic enormous helmet from the original film and walked through the packed house at Hall H of the San Diego Convention Center.
The crowd couldn’t help but give Moranis, who stepped back from appearing in films almost three decades ago, a standing ovation.

The sequel, entitled “Spaceballs: The New One,” is slated to hit theaters on April 23, 2027. The project was championed by several comedians and actors including Josh Gad. It will feature some familiar faces, like the original film’s director Mel Brooks, who is not only a producer on the sequel but also reprising his role as the beloved Yoda parody character Yogurt.

Moranis’ entrance was certainly a theatrical one. The actor did not begin the event with the rest of the panel. Rather, he surprised the crowd by popping up in the audience after being hidden under the helmet. The crowd, understandably, went wild.
Moranis, who then joined the panel, told fans about his decision to reenter the industry with the upcoming film.
“It just felt like this is it. It’s time,” he told the crowd. “I said yes, and it is the best decision I’ve ever made.”
The actor, whose reprisal of the beloved villain role was announced last year, also joked that he had never really left.  He said that he had discussed the idea of a sequel way back in 1989.
“I wasn’t really retired,” he joked. “I was just negotiating.”
The panel was filled with several other noteworthy moments, including a parody of the Marvel Cinematic Universe, the universe of Marvel superhero films that are typically released in “phases.”
For this event, the panel unveiled the “Spaceballs Cinematic Universe.” The MCU spoof included upwards of 11 phases including “The Almighty Schwartz Saga.” (IYKYK!)
Though Mel Brooks did not attend the event, he sent along a hilarious video message.

“Sorry I can’t be with you. I’m on the convention floor trying to buy a rare Charizard card. When I was your age, on a Friday, I would go to something called ‘work,’” he said in the video, according to Deadline. “From the bottom of my heart I want to say, thank you, nerds.”

title: Conan O’Brien Addresses His Shocking New Hair: ‘I’m One Of The Thunderbirds That Is Easily 55’
summary: Comedian Conan O’Brien, who’s known for his very red, very high pompadour, recently stepped out with a shockingly different hairstyle. And in a new video clip, he explained why.
story: Comedian Conan O’Brien, who’s known for his very red, very high pompadour, recently stepped out with a shockingly different hairstyle. And now viewers finally understand why.

O’Brien, 63, addressed the new look in a July 22 clip from his podcast “Conan O’Brien Needs A Friend.” Fans had first spotted the makeover during an episode of the podcast, which featured fellow comedian Molly Shannon, earlier that same week. It prompted many a question about the departure from his signature style.

The origin story, it turns out, begins at the June 18 opening of the Obama Presidential Center in Chicago, which O’Brien attended. The comedian explained on the clip that he originally did not realize that the event was outdoors. While he splashed a bit of sunblock on his face, the story would later take a turn.

“It’s three hours plus, and when it’s over, I’m so glad that I put the sunblock on, and I’m feeling really good about myself,” O’Brien said in the clip, joking that he felt superior to others like comedians David Letterman and Stephen Colbert, who did not appear to have prepared like he did. “I’m like, ‘Well, those suckers don’t know how to put sunblock on.’”
The good vibes did not last for long.

“A day or two later, after the event, I feel like my skull is on fire. And then two days after that, my skull is really itchy, and whenever I itch it, it looks like a snow globe,” he said. “White freckled confetti is pouring off of my head. It’s disgusting.”
It turns out that O’Brien suffered a pretty bad sunburn on his scalp.

“I talked to someone. They said, ‘Yeah, you got a sunburn on your scalp,’ which I’m not used to because I’ve got so much hair, but this sun just blasted right through my hair, and it roasted my scalp,” O’Brien explained. “To treat this, you’ve got to rub oil into it.”
The comedian admitted that while treating the burn, he had forgotten that he had podcast duties later that same day.
“Then I come in and I look like I’m in Sha Na Na. I’m a grease ball,” O’Brien said, referencing the doo-wop revival band.
Of course, he and his co-host Sona Movsesian and assistant David Hopping could not help but have a little fun with the new ‘do.
“I look like I want to fight one of you in the parking lot by swinging a chain at you in 1952, or a little switchblade,” O’Brien said.
O’Brien also joked that he looked like “one of the Thunderbirds that is easily 55 years old” in the 1978 film “Grease.”
Before he even addressed the hair, fans had been roasting O’Brien over the look.
“Seeing Conan’s hair like this feels illegal,” one social media user wrote.
Another person dubbed O’Brien “Coney Soprano,” a riff on “The Sopranos” mobster Tony Soprano.

title: Meghan Markle’s ‘Summer Holiday’ Snaps With Kids Include a Visit to Princess Diana’s Childhood Home
summary: Meghan Markle shared photos from her, Prince Harry and their kids summer vacation, which included time at the beach and Princess Diana’s family estate.
story: Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, has been soaking up the sun, enjoying the company of her family, and remembering loved ones this summer.
In a series of photos posted July 23 on Instagram, the former Meghan Markle shared a look at her recent vacation with husband Prince Harry and their children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet.
Among the snaps include a black-and-white photo of her and Harry laughing during a meal, Harry flipping Lilibet in the pool, Archie in the pilot seat of an airplane and Meghan with her pup.
However, there is one photo in particular that has captured people’s attention: the family visiting Princess Diana’s childhood home.
The photo shows Harry and Archie carrying large bouquets, with Lilibet behind them as they walk down a grassy yard. The location is believed to be taken at Althorp, the late royal’s family estate.

Located in Northamptonshire, England, the Spencer family 13,000 acre estate is where Princess Diana is buried on a secluded island in the Round Oval lake. While the estate is open to the public, the burial site is off-limits.

Princess Diana’s brother and Harry’s uncle, Charles Spencer, lives at Althorp, meaning the family could have spent time with him while at the estate. On the Althorp website, it notes that the establishment was closed July 10 and 11.

Earlier this month, Harry traveled to the U.K. for a series of public events, including promoting the 2027 Invictus Games. He was joined by Meghan and their kids, who did not make any public appearances.
The family, however, did reunite with King Charles III, marking the first time he had seen his grandchildren in four years.
Buckingham Palace confirmed to NBC News on July 10 that the king and Queen Camilla hosted Harry, Meghan, Archie and Lilibet at Highgrove House, their private residence in Gloucestershire, England.
The last time the children saw their grandfather was in 2022 when they attended Queen Elizabeth II’s Platinum Jubilee, celebrating her 70 years on the throne.
Another snap that is making people nostalgic is one where the former “Suits” star is wearing a black one-piece bathing suit and watching her family getting into the ocean.
The shot was reminiscent of Princess Diana’s previous beach vacations, with her wearing similar swimwear.

Over the years, Meghan has honored her late mother-in-law with her style choices. Some have been more meaningful, including wearing Princess Diana’s jewelry, including her butterfly earrings and bracelet.

Other times, Meghan’s past outfits have drawn comparisons to Harry’s mother’s looks. One instance was in 2020 when the former actor wore a green dress and fascinator, with people comparing it to Diana’s 1982 Trooping the Colour outfit.

title: The Best New Books of 2026, According to TODAY  Guests

story: If you’re looking for books to read, beyond the latest Read With Jenna picks, you’re in the right place. Throughout the year, authors stop by TODAY to share the books they’re reading and loving lately.

July 2026
"The MASH Up" by Laurie Marie Meyers
A rom-com about a woman who wakes up on her 35th birthday and is trapped in a game she created as a teen.

What John Searles said: “For fans of ‘13 Going on 30’ comes Laura Marie Meyers’ sparkling and laugh-out-loud funny romantic comedy about a woman who wakes up the morning after her 35th birthday to find that she is trapped inside a game of MASH that she created in the 7th Grade. This hits the millennial sweet spot and is a fun read.”
"Dominion" by Jean Kwok
The first book apart of Kwok's new fantasy series.

What John Searles said: “‘Fourth Wing’ — by way of Chinese mythology — meets ‘The Hunger Games’ in a perilous world where a young woman with no memory and little magic may hold the key to uniting the Dominions and saving the mortal realm, the first in The Silk and Iron trilogy, from the New York Times bestselling author of Read With Jenna pick ‘Searching for Sylvie Lee’ and ‘Girl in Translation.’”
"Helpless" by Jessica Knoll
A woman who attends her college professor's funeral is kidnapped by her ex-boyfriend in this twisty thriller.

What John Searles said: “A successful Hollywood producer returns to her college alma mater and is reunited with her volatile, obsessive ex-boyfriend. What begins as an unsettling chance encounter spirals into a dark, twisty erotic thriller when Henry drugs and kidnaps her, forcing Faye to confront years-old secrets and the true, dangerous nature of their twisted past. Juicy and fun and full of twists.”
"The Odyssey" by Homer
The greek classic.

What John said: “It seems so surprising to me but the classic Greek poem we all had to study in college is being released as one of summer’s biggest movies, starring Anne Hathaway and Matt Damon and Tom Holland. Directed by Christopher Nolan, the film was shot entirely on IMAX cameras in breathtaking locations like Greece, Iceland and Italy. It stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, Tom Holland as Telemachus, and Zendaya as Athena.”
June 2026
"Phoebe Berman's Gonna Lose It" by Brooke Averick
A funny, warm story about a hopeless romantic determined to lose her virginity before her 30th birthday.

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “‘Phoebe Berman’s Gonna Lose It’ is oh so warm and deeply charming — a novel about romance, friendship, anxiety, and the strange little deadlines we invent for becoming ourselves. In this case, well, losing one’s virginity before turning 30. Laugh-out-loud funny while still being tender and big-hearted, here is a love story in the truest sense, about learning to want honestly, messily and entirely on your own terms.”
"Main Characters: A Novel" by Bobby Palmer
A love story of a pair whose paths unexpectedly cross throughout two decades, told from outside perspectives.

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “Main Characters’ is a brilliant book — a captivating love story told from the margins by the people who perhaps understand us before we understand ourselves. The book follows Clara and Seb across two decades as their lives brush up against one another’s, but is told from the perspective of everyone around them. A clever concept that totally works, here is a great summer read for anyone who has ever believed in the life-changing power of truly being seen.”
"This Vast Enterprise: A New History of Lewis & Clark" by Craig Fehrman
After years of research, this is an entertaining history of US history's two famous explorers.

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “An incredible feat, Craig Fehrman’s ‘This Vast Enterprise’ is a wildly entertaining history of Lewis and Clark — the product of more than half a decade of rigorous and immensely impressive research — that never loses sight of the adventure at its center. Fehrman brings this legendary expedition thrillingly to life by turning our attention beyond Lewis and Clark themselves, revealing the oft-overlooked people and perspectives that made the journey possible. Expansive, compelling, and alive on every page, this is a perfect summer read for America’s 250th anniversary.”
"The Art of Loving You" by Natasha Bishop
The sequel to Bishop's "Only for the Week" of an intimate, spicy romance set during a bucket list road trip.

What Yasmine Cheyenne said: “Impossible to put down, this romance winds you through love, loss and the joy thats possible on the other side of change. If you love a plot that moves you as much as it inspires you, this is your pick!’
"Love by the Book: A Novel" by Jessica George
An honest story about the complications of adult friendships and new connections.

What Yasmine Cheyenne said: “A page-turner that puts words to what so many of us quietly feel about adult friendships — the growing pains, the unexpected shifts, and the beauty of who finds you in the in-between.”
"Waiting on a Friend: A Novel" by Natalie Adler
A story about friendship and community during a time of defiance and loss.

What Yasmine Cheyenne said: “A debut that somehow makes you feel more alive the deeper it pulls you into loss — an absolute love letter to a moment in history that still echoes today, with all the heart and humor to prove it.”
May 2026
"The Lost Book of Lancelot" by John Glynn

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “This is a wildly entertaining retelling of the King Arthur myth, focusing on the life of Lancelot through a lense of queer exploration. Glynn does a fantastic job blending historical elements alongside adventure and fantasy. Filled with incredible world building, Glynn’s writing shines as he explores the Arthurian era with authority, and breathes new life into these long-known legends.”
"Famesick: A Memoir" by Lena Dunham

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “’Famesick’ is the singular memoir from a singular voice — famously ‘a voice of a generation,’ as the line on her show ‘Girls’ goes — and polarizing figure in millennial culture, Lena Dunham. But you don’t have to be a GIRLS fan to enjoy this marvelous memoir. For starters, it’s rare to get a celebrity memoir this dishy and confessional, this genuinely shocking, sure. But also, you rarely if ever get them this well-written. You can feel how much care and craft went into this book, how much intelligence and skill, which is why it’s getting the response it’s getting, and why it is likely to stick around well past the news cycle.”
"Burnout Summer" by Jenna Ramirez

What Isaac Fitzgerald said: “’Burnout Summer’ follows the story of Camille Luna, a young woman who has just gotten out of a night in jail for some small crimes after losing her job and spiraling. Camille is picked up by an old friend, Danny, who whisks her off to his beachside hometown in Rhode Island, saving her for the summer from her flailing, corporate life in Washington DC. What ensues is an utterly spectacular will-they-or-won’t-they where the guy is delightfully straightforward and has his life together and the girl is the messy one. Ramirez’s sparkling writing makes the beach town come to life on the page — you can almost smell the sea salt in the air — a perfect blend of escapism and romance.”
April 2026
"Escape!" by Stephen Fishbach
Stephen Fishbach survived “Survivor” twice and wrote a novel inspired by his experiences. For Straub, a “Survivor” fan, this book is all a person could ask for.
“This is a novel about a reality TV program based on ‘Survivor.’ He’s a really smart, funny writer,” Emma Straub said.
"The Reservation" by Rebecca Kauffman

Emma Straub likens “Reservation” to “bingeing a whole season of ‘The Bear.’” It’s an “immersive novel” set over the course of one day at a small restaurant in a college town, she says. The headline news in the restaurant? John Grisham has made a reservation and everything needs to be perfect.
"The Fountain" by Casey Scieszka
Vera Van Valkenburgh has returned home for the first time in 128 years. After enjoying the fruits of the fountain of youth, Vera is tired and ready for a release.
“We need more contemporary novels with fantastical elements,” Emma Straub said. “This is a debut, smart and fun. Immortality in the Hudson Valley!”
"This Is Not About Us" by Allegra Goodman
Filled with humor, this is a story about growing old and the love that connects a family across generations.

How is it possible that an apple pie could cause a years-long rift between sisters? After Sylvia and Helen Rubinstein’s sister passes away, their relationship is in turmoil, enough so that a baked good could cause a major problem.
Coben calls this his “favorite novel of the year” so far.
"The Left And The Lucky" by Willy Vlautin
This text is an honest display of the power of friendship and how, in various ways, it can save our lives.

“The Left and the Lucky” is the latest from an author who is known for his portraits of contemporary American life. In this one, a young boy befriends his next-door neighbor, offering him an escape from his tumultuous family life.
Coben calls this book “gut-wrenching” and “compassionate,” with shades of John Steinbeck. There’s “dignity and integrity” in this working-class story, he says.
"Mad Mabel" by Sally Hepworth
Mad Mabel is a funny, inspiring, story of an underestimated woman about to prove everyone wrong.
At 15, Elsie Fitzpatrick became Australia’s youngest convicted murderer. Now 81, Elsie has left that behind her — until a young girl moves in across the road and unearths her past.
“Sally Hepworth is a huge star in Australia. This is the book that’s going to make her a huge star here,” Harlan Coben said on TODAY. He calls this book “funny, twisty and suspenseful.”
March 2026
"Imperfect Women" by Araminta Hall
This psychological thriller explores guilt, retribution, love and betrayal through three fascinating perspectives.

Nancy Hennessy is murdered and leaves behind a secret: The identity of a lover who nobody knew about. Not her husband. Not her friends. Not her daughter. The adaptation is soon to air on AppleTV+ starring Elisabeth Moss and Kerry Washington.
"Where the Wildflowers Grow" by Terah Shelton Harris
Be inspired by Terah Shelton Harris' newest story of survival and redemption.

“Where the Wildflowers Grow’ opens with a harrowing scene: A prison bus crashes over a ravine leaving only one survivor. Leigh survives and runs away to a flower farm in rural Alabama, starting a tale of hope and redemption.
"That's What Friends Are For" by Wade Rouse
Inspired by The Golden Girls, this hilarious story celebrates love, aging, and finding your people.

Fans of “The Golden Girls” will love this book inspired by the show about friendship and aging in style. Theodore Copeland’s estranged sister and her granddaughter show up at his oasis in Palm Springs, bringing secrets and disruption to his life with the “Golden Gays” (his nickname for his friend group).
"Python's Kiss: Stories" by Louise Erdrich
Explore Louise Erdrich’s writing with this magnificent collection of her stories.

Louise Erdrich, whose last book was chosen for Read With Jenna’s book club, has a new collection of short stories written from the past two decades of her storied career. According to the description from the publisher, the story collection features characters like “a tribal newsletter editor whose son tells her a story that nothing in her experience can encompass” and a girl who decides to spend her life with a stone.
February 2026
"And Now, Back to You" by B.K. Borison

What Julia Quinn said: “I’m not saying B.K. Borison has magic powers, but it’s a little suspicious that her romance novel about two meteorologists stranded together during the storm of the century is landing in bookstores right now... as half the country is clearing out from the storm of the century. Seriously though, ‘And Now, Back to You’ is simply delightful in every way. The characters are charming and real, and the book manages to make you laugh and tug on your heartstrings. Five stars, all the way.”
"Keeper of Lost Children" by Sadeqa Johnson

What Julia Quinn said: “I love when fiction introduces me to a piece of history I never knew about, and ‘Keeper of Lost Children’ does just that by shining a light on the true story of the ‘Brown Baby Plan,’ a 1950s movement spearheaded by African-American journalist Mabel Grammer to bring biracial children of white German women and Black American GIs to the United States for adoption.’ In Keeper of Lost Children,’ Mabel has been fictionalized as Ethel Gathers, who has moved to Germany with her husband, who is an officer in the US Army. She is shocked when she discovers hundreds of biracial babies living in German orphanages and, after adopting several children herself, begins a one-woman mission to find homes for the rest. I loved everything about this book, from the impeccably researched plot to the beautifully-drawn characters.”
"Project Hail Mary" by Andy Weir

What Julia Quinn said: “I loved ‘The Martian,’ both on page and screen, so it was a no brainer for me to pick this up. Andy Weir puts a lot of science in his science fiction, but he also spins a terrific story with compelling characters, including our protagonist, Ryland Grace, a middle school science teacher who is somehow tasked with saving the world from a climate fueled apocalypse. Fortunately for humanity, Ryland soon teams up with Rocky, an alien life-form who’s a bit like a metallic spider (but with a heart of gold and a keen sense of sarcasm). The stakes in this novel are sky high, but Weir keeps the story grounded with geeky humor, and it’s easy to see why ‘Project Hail Mary’ is predicted to be one of the biggest blockbuster movies of 2026.”
"How to Commit a Postcolonial Murder" by Nina McConigley

What Julia Quinn said: “Every now and then I pick up a book solely because I’m intrigued by the title. What is a postcolonial murder? And why do I want to know how to commit one? Georgie Ayyar Creel is a 12-year-old Indian-American child, who, along with her sister Agatha, are navigating girlhood in a very white Wyoming town where ‘Indian’ usually means Native American. Their lives are upended by the arrival of their uncle Vinny, who emigrates from India with his family. Vinny molests them, repeatedly, and the two girls decide to poison him slowly with antifreeze. I thought this books would be a mystery, and in some ways it is, but is much more a tale of girlhood, and sisterhood, and all the ways a family bond can fracture. Georgie’s narration is wry and sharp, often speaking directly to the reader, and in this way, we are forced to reckon with her choices as if they were our own. ‘How to Commit a Postcolonial Murder’ is the kind of book that is difficult to describe, but so very easy to recommend.”
Quinn also shared a list of books she read and enjoyed for the rest of the year:

January 2026
"Behind These Four Walls" by Yasmin Angoe

What Brad Thor said: “Ten years after her best friend vanishes, a woman poses as a journalist to infiltrate the wealthy family connected to her disappearance. Every answer raises a worse question — was her friend a victim, or was she playing a deeper game?”
"Drive Me Crazy" by Lizzy Dent

What Brad Thor said: “Like an even steamier version of the Brad Pitt movie ‘F1.’ She’s an up-and-coming Formula 1 team principal. He’s her new hotshot driver — and her childhood crush — so their careers depend on working together without blowing up the team or each other. It’s high-speed romance with stakes you instantly get.”
"The Viper" by Brad Meltzer
What Brad Thor said: “A dying man hides something priceless inside the suit he plans to be buried in — then he’s murdered for it. It’s a killer premise with a personal gut-punch payoff!”
"People We Meet on Vacation" by Emily Henry

What Brad Thor said: “Best friends, polar opposites, years of summer trips — and the one question they’ve avoided: are they actually meant to be together? Read the book now, then watch the Netflix adaptation drop January 9. It’s your perfect ‘book first, binge next’ pick.”
"Mattering" by Jennifer Breheny Wallace

What Brad Thor said: “A lot of people don’t need another goal — they need to feel like they actually count. Mattering goes straight at the quiet stuff driving burnout and drift: feeling invisible, disconnected, and stuck on autopilot. Wallace lays out concrete ways to rebuild connection and purpose — so the New Year isn’t just a reset of your calendar, it’s a reset of your life.”

title: Darlene Love is Turning 85! Her Tips For Staying Forever Young
summary: Acclaimed soul singer and Christmas holiday icon Darlene Love has a gift for staying young. Here’s her longevity and health tips.
story: Acclaimed soul singer and Christmas holiday icon Darlene Love has a gift for staying young.

Love, who stopped by TODAY on July 24 to promote her upcoming documentary “Darlene Love: I Know Where I’ve Been,”  will be turning 85 years old on July 26. The songstress, who still continues to perform live, has opened up in the past about the many keys to her remarkably active lifestyle. But one of the most important secrets boils down to a particular mindset, she said on the show.
“You know what?” she told TODAY’s Al Roker, Dylan Dreyer and  Savannah Sellers. “I love life!”
Love also joked on the show that her youthfulness sometimes makes for awkward moments while out with family.
“I have a son who is 65,” Love said. “And they think they’re my boyfriends.”

The octogenarian has been lighting up the stage and screen for decades now. Born Darlene Wright, Love first got a taste of fame as a member of 1960s background vocals girl group The Blossoms. As part of the successful trio, Love sang with big acts like Elvis, Frank Sinatra, Dionne Warwick and many more. The three, which included Fanita James, and Jean King, even provided backing vocals to the Halloween hit “The Monster Mash.”

Love would go on to further make a name for herself with her 1963 classic “Christmas (Baby Please Come Home),” a track that is often in regular rotation around the holidays. Her extensive decadeslong body of work landed her a place in the Rock & Roll Hall of Fame in 2011.

Love’s talents extended to the silver screen as well. She played main character Roger Murtaugh’s wife, Trish, in the “Lethal Weapon” film series. She’s also graced the Broadway stage as Motormouth Maybelle in “Hairspray.”

The soon-to-be-85-year-old doesn’t appear to be slowing down, either. And she’s been known for not only her electrifying performances, but also for doing them in 6-inch stilettos. For the multi-hyphenate, she’s said her youthfulness has to do with several factors, including a whole lot of rest.

“Sleep a minimum of six to eight hours. Your rest is very important because this profession is very grueling,” Love told the Digital Journal in a 2025 interview ahead of her Christmas tour later that year. “They say our 90-minute set is equivalent of a man working eight hours; that’s the amount of energy we expel,”
She also underscores the importance of staying active.

“You have to take care of your body, and I’ve always done that,” Love told the Digital Journal. “Right now, I’ll be 84 in a few weeks, I get up at 5 a.m. five days a week and I do a kickboxing class.”
Love also told the outlet that sometimes, she even walks the length of the Mario M. Cuomo Bridge in Rockland County, New York, where she lives.
“You really do have to keep yourself active,” she said. “Even when you are not working, you can’t just sit around and do nothing.”
Love has said in the past, she’s just thankful to be able to continue to do what she loves — performing.

“I thank God every day for my health, the fact that I still have my voice 🎤, I can walk, talk, and move like I’m in my 40s (okay, maybe 50s 😄)” Love wrote in a social media post in celebration of her 84th birthday. “Whether it’s good genes, pure luck, or just taking care of myself, I’m not questioning it. I’m just grateful 🙏🏽”

title: Didi Conn, 75, Re-Creates Her Frenchy Outfit for ‘Grease’ Show
summary: Didi Conn, who played Frenchy in the movie “Grease,” made an appearance at “Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical” in London.
story: One of Rydell High’s most famous students has returned to the school.
Didi Conn, who played Frenchy in the classic 1978 movie “Grease,” made an appearance at the July 23 London performance of “Grease: The Immersive Movie Musical.”
Conn, 75, wore a Pink Ladies jacket and fought back tears while wiping her eyes when “Beauty School Dropout” was sung during the show.
The actor also shared her wisdom on how to be a Pink Lady in a video posted on the show’s Instagram page.
“In order to be a Pink Lady, you gotta act cool, you gotta look cool, and you gotta be cool ‘til death do us part,” she said.
“And, think pink! Pink is the color of love. Just think about if you’re ever feeling lonely, there’s a big, warm, cozy, fuzzy pink blanket of love just hugging you,” she added.
Conn also met the show’s director, Matt Costain, and some of the stars, who asked her if she had any advice about being a Pink Lady.
“No, just love each other. That’s all. We really loved each other, except for Rizzo,” she joked, alluding to the tough leader of the group, played in the movie by Stockard Channing.
“I’m blown away by this,” she added. “All of you are perfect.”
Conn, who would later star on the sitcom “Benson” and the children’s series “Shining Time Station,” may have gotten a sign that the role of Frenchy was meant to be.

“My agent said, ‘You gotta go looking like the character,’” she said in a June 30 Instagram video about her audition for the part. “And all I knew was that her name was Frenchy. I did know that she wanted to be a beautician. And I’m driving home and what do I see, but Frenchy’s Beauty Parlor.”
Conn said she stopped into the shop and treated herself to a new hairdo.

“And Little Frenchy, she did my hair with at least two cans of spray,” she recalled. “I had a big hairdo and I learned so much about beauty school. And when I went to the audition, I told them the story about Frenchy. They told me later, as soon as I opened my mouth I had the role. I didn’t know that.”

title: Chris Anne Affleck, Civil Rights Organizer And Mother of Ben and Casey Affleck, Dies at 83
summary: Christopher Anne Affleck, mother of Ben and Casey Affleck, died in June after a monthslong battle with a terminal illness, according to her obituary.
story: Christopher Anne Affleck, mother of actors Ben and Casey Affleck, died in June after a monthslong battle with a terminal illness, the family announced July 23. She was 83.

Affleck, a civil rights organizer and teacher, received her diagnosis in December 2025 and was given six months to live, according to her obituary in The Boston Globe. She passed just after being able to witness one of her biggest ambitions, according to the family.

“Her greatest wish after her diagnosis, however, was to live to see her grandson graduate high school,” the family wrote in the obituary. “She did so, attending with her family on May 31, 2026. She died peacefully, in her sleep, two days later.”
Affleck, who was born in New York City in 1942, spent 35 years as a public school teacher in Massachusetts, the obituary said.
“Every student, whether just arrived from Haiti or Cambridge upper crust, was a cherished citizen of her classroom republic, equal to each other and to herself,” the family wrote in the tribute.

A Harvard graduate, Affleck also spent a large part of her life involved in civil rights movements. During Freedom Summer — a 1964 summer initiative aimed at raising awareness around violence against the Black community and increasing voter registration and political participation — Affleck got involved, teaching literacy classes, according to the obituary. An active participant in 1960s counterculture, Affleck also marched against the Vietnam War, the tribute said.
The family wrote in the obituary that Affleck’s unique, revolutionary spirit was present in her life since childhood.
“From the beginning of her life, Chris made her unconventional name her own, foreshadowing both the personality and the practicality that would follow her to her death,” the obituary said.

Affleck, the commemoration said, grew up idolizing her stepfather Sam, who was a World War II veteran and a civil rights supporter. During her years at all-girls private school Nightingale-Bamford, Affleck “made the most of an elite education while remaining skeptical of the tightly cloistered world it represented,” the obituary said.

In one particular instance, the obituary said, a teacher had chastised Affleck for her criticism of Jim Crow — the laws and policies that enforced racial segregation primarily from 1877 to the mid-1960s — without hearing the “other side.”
